Hi Kelly — great to hear from you and glad the demo resonated. Attached are two artifacts to answer your questions: an attached pricing workbook (optimize_pricing_sheet.xlsx) and a compact engineering note with quantization guidance (quant_recs.pdf). High level reply below, plus a suggested MAP.

Pricing & packaging (summary):
- Starter — 100k Optimize credits + 4 hours onboarding: good for POC and baseline tuning. No commitment.
- Growth — 1M credits committed (12mo) + 8 hours onboarding + 1 playbook review: discounted unit pricing vs Starter. Typical customers see ~30–40% lower per-token cost vs on-demand when they adopt batching/caching and recommended quantization.
- Enterprise — committed credits + Dedicated tier (optional) + extended support and SLAs. We can carve deeper concessions for 12–24 month commits.

Quantization & expected economics (short):
- Recommendation: start with an int8 (GPTQ/NM) profile on non-critical model tails; validate on your eval set. For many transformer encoder/decoder variants, INT8 quant with a small calibration set yields 1.8–3.0x CPU/GPU throughput improvement and roughly 2–2.5x lower token cost vs FP16 serving when combined with batching and KV caching.
- For generative head models, try NF4 or gptq-int8 first — preserves quality for prompts up to 512 tokens in our tests. Critical: run a small A/B (1000 prompts) against your user-facing prompts to measure metric drift (perplexity / BLEU / any task-specific metric).
- Fallback policy: we recommend keeping an FP16 variant as a fallback for high-sensitivity queries; Redwood can route by policy (confidence or prompt tag).

Batching & caching guidance (short):
- Latency SLOs: use micro-batching with dynamic queue timeouts (we typically batch 8–32 requests depending on target p99). For your 40–60ms p95 targets on search recall, start with batch_size=8 and measure tail latency.
- Prefix/KV caching: cache recent session KV prefixes (customer side warmup + server-side prefix caching). For short-context workloads this reduced effective token compute by ~18–28% in our benchmarks.

Trial & MAP: happy to offer a 60k credit trial + 4 hours of onboarding (SRE + solutions). Attached is a one-page MAP template (also included in the pricing sheet) with milestones: trial deploy (week 1), eval window (week 2–3), negotiation/PO (week 4).

Attachments: [Attachment: optimize_pricing_sheet.xlsx (xlsx)], [Attachment: quant_recs.pdf (pdf)]

Next steps: if you’re comfortable with the initial MAP I’ll loop in our Sales Ops and Legal to prepare a simple commitment term and an initial PO path. Happy to tailor the commitment band to hit your unit-cost target — do you have a target per-token spend we should aim for?

Thanks,
